nameStory: The name "delta mudwort" comes from this tiny plant's love of muddy places, especially the triangular delta areas where rivers meet larger bodies of water. The "wort" part is an old English word meaning "plant," often used for small, humble plants that early herbalists thought had medicinal value.
description: Delta mudwort is a tiny annual plant that forms small patches in muddy shores and tidal flats. This diminutive member of the figwort family grows as a low, creeping mat with small spoon-shaped leaves. The entire plant rarely grows taller than your thumb, making it easy to overlook among the mud and debris of shorelines. Despite its small size, it produces delicate white flowers that bloom from summer into fall.

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Forms low, creeping mats directly on mud or wet sand, with the entire plant staying very close to the ground like a living carpet

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Small, spoon-shaped leaves that feel smooth and slightly succulent, arranged in tiny rosettes emerging from the muddy surface

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Tiny white flowers, each smaller than a pencil eraser, sitting close to the mud surface on very short stalks

idTips.label: Habitat Context
idTips.description: Always found directly in or on wet mud, never in grassy areas or dry soil, often with your feet sinking slightly as you observe it

habitat: Look for delta mudwort on tidal mudflats, muddy pond edges, and sandy shores where the ground stays consistently moist or wet. It thrives in areas that flood regularly, particularly along coastal estuaries and the muddy margins of freshwater bodies. You'll often find it mixed with other small wetland plants in spots where most larger plants can't establish.

seasonality.spring: Young plants begin emerging as small green rosettes in the warming mud, often barely visible among shoreline debris.
seasonality.summer: Plants reach full size and begin blooming, with tiny white flowers appearing close to the mud surface from July onward.
seasonality.fall: Continues flowering through early fall, with plants becoming more noticeable as other vegetation dies back, revealing the small green mats.
seasonality.winter: Annual plants die completely, leaving no trace above ground until seeds germinate the following spring.

funFact: This tiny plant is tough enough to handle saltwater flooding during high tides, then switch gears and thrive in fresh rainwater - it's like a botanical amphibian that can live in both worlds!
confusionNotes: The small size and muddy habitat make it unlikely to be confused with most other plants, but beginners might overlook it entirely, mistaking it for algae or moss growing on the mud surface. Remember: if you see tiny white flowers in the mud, you've found mudwort!
contextualKnowledge: Despite being called "Welsh mudwort" in some references, this species is actually native to North America, not Wales. The naming confusion likely comes from its similarity to European mudwort species that early botanists were more familiar with.
compareHints: Delta mudwort is the only mudwort species commonly found in New England, making identification easier once you recognize the genus. Compared to other tiny plants in the figwort family, mudworts are unique in their extreme preference for muddy, frequently flooded habitats where most other figworts cannot survive.
